analysis.title: Fixed Income Monthly: Midterms sharpen the focus on fiscal risk (November 2026)
key_insights: The Democratic midterm victory adds uncertainty around US fiscal, trade and regulatory policy. Fixed income has reacted little so far, but the size of the gains could matter through next year's budget and debt-ceiling negotiations and potential implications for data-centre investment.

The US 10-year Treasury yield fell about 35bps to 4.94% in October after September's sell-off. Fidelity attributes the move to safe-haven demand amid technology weakness and AI investment concerns, not a decisive improvement in the inflation outlook.

The US economy remains resilient with private demand holding up. Recent PCE revisions do not change the picture, higher energy prices add inflation risk, and tentative consumer weakness needs confirmation from official data. World Cup-related effects may have distorted recent activity.

The Fed held in October. Fidelity keeps its December hike call and says markets may be underestimating further tightening. The midterms do not change that near-term view but raise medium-term fiscal uncertainty.

Fidelity trimmed long-duration exposure, particularly in Europe, while keeping a modest long rates bias. AI-related equity weakness tightened financial conditions and restored some diversification benefit to government bonds, but yields are now closer to macro-justified levels.

Europe faces higher energy prices, euro weakness and persistent inflation, which keep pressure on the ECB. French fiscal and political concerns drove substantial sovereign spread widening. Fidelity reduced European duration and favours differentiation across countries.
Credit is showing strong dispersion after resilience during the rates sell-off. Fidelity changed portfolio credit beta and credit-quality selection.
Overall stance is selective risk-taking. Duration is held as protection against a sharper slowdown, and wider credit dispersion offers opportunities without a broad increase in portfolio risk.

Macro and unconstrained: modestly long duration after profit-taking, favouring Australian and UK government bonds, selective German Bunds, underweight France and Italy, long US inflation, long US dollar bias, closed remaining yen and Australian dollar shorts, cautious on credit.

Global IG moved to neutral: sound fundamentals and attractive yields are offset by tight valuations, growing AI-related supply and regional dispersion. Selective opportunities in European financials and corporate hybrids after spread widening. Cautious on Euro IG, balanced on Sterling IG, selective on US and Asia IG.
Global IG returned 1.6% in October despite spreads widening 11bps. US IG outperformed European credit, and French sovereign volatility weighed on Euro IG with some spillover to peripheral markets.

High yield: slightly negative on US HY (tight valuations, rising financing needs) and European HY (rising rates, heavy new-issue pipeline), neutral on Asian HY. CCC-rated US bonds underperformed in October, and Asian HY fell on Chinese property concerns and Indonesian volatility.

Emerging markets: neutral on hard currency sovereigns and corporates. Cautious near term on local duration and EM FX because of persistent dollar strength, while constructive long term. A surprise Brazilian election result caused a sharp sell-off in Brazilian government bonds and a weaker real.
UK inflation rose from 3.1% to 3.5%, with energy an important driver. Australia's housing downturn gathered momentum.

sector_views.rationale: Sound fundamentals and attractive yields are balanced by tight valuations, AI-related supply and regional dispersion.
Tight valuations and rising financing needs outweigh higher income, solid earnings and controlled leverage. Stance is slightly negative.
Rising rates, a difficult macro backdrop and a heavy new-issue pipeline outweigh higher yields and subdued defaults. Stance is slightly negative.
Attractive carry and improving valuations are balanced by Treasury volatility and the need for selectivity.
Selective opportunities rather than broad beta amid uncertainty and richer valuations.

tension_points.bull_case: Weakness in risk assets and AI investment concerns restore government bonds' diversification benefit, and duration protects against a sharper slowdown.
tension_points.bear_case: Resilient activity, sticky inflation, higher energy prices and further Fed tightening could push yields higher, and markets may underprice tightening.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weakness in risk assets broadening into the economy would favour duration, while resilient activity and inflation again pushing yields higher would break the long rates bias.
